newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds close higher, calm.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds close higher, calm.

text.p: Argentine bonds recorded gains at the close Thursday but slipped off the day's highs in a relaxed trading environment, dealers said.

"There was no frenzy here today, despite the sharp gains in U.S. Treasuries," one dealer said. "This shows our market is still somewhat overbought and players here are confident but in no rush to build up their positions."
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/8 to 94-1/2, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 added $0.10 to 121.50.
"Volume improved ahead of the long weekend in the U.S. but tomorrow should be very dull, with prices flat to firm," another dealer said, referring to Friday's Independence Day holiday.

Traders said the favorable U.S. jobs report Friday, which came on the heels of the Federal Reserve's decision not to touch interest rates, set the stage for fresh gains in fixed income markets next week.
